per_pair.why: A's start reads immediately through a forward lean, trailing scarf and dust puffs, and it snaps back to idle within a frame or two of stopping, while B's camera pans so much that the run itself is harder to read.

B's reversals flip between two clean, readable facing poses, while A rotates its voxel model through muddy in-between angles (a front-facing frame, a sword swinging wide) that make each turn look slower and messier.
A's camera keeps the character steadily framed through all eight directions with a clear facing on each leg, while B's camera drifts and reframes heavily partway through the box.

B's dash covers a large distance in one or two frames with a bold, high-contrast smear and a clean landing pose, while A's dash is short and its teal afterimage is muted and blends into the dark floor.
B's character stays pinned to the wall in a stable, high-contrast pose as it slides, while A's blue-on-blue sprite nearly disappears against the wall and its silhouette changes between frames.

loser_biggest_gap: Make the dash land as one decisive event. Cover clearly more ground in 1-2 frames, and leave a bright, high-contrast smear or afterimage that stands out against the dark floor (not a muted teal). End it on a clean recovery pose, so it reads as a burst instead of a slightly faster run.
loser_other_gaps: Snap facing changes on reversals and 8-way turns to the new direction within a frame, instead of showing the voxel model rotating through in-between angles such as the front-facing frame mid-reversal.

Increase the character's contrast against the floor and walls with a rim light, outline or brighter cloak value, so its silhouette stays readable while moving fast, especially when pressed against a wall.
Keep the sword and scarf poses consistent from frame to frame during a run and a wall slide; the sword angle jumps around and makes the silhouette noisy.
Add a short skid or settle pose with a dust burst on hard stops and reversals, so changes of direction show weight as well as speed.
reasoning: Both sides start and stop quickly, and A's camera actually frames its character more steadily than B's, which drifts and pans a lot. What B does better is make each action read. Its turns snap to clean facing poses, its dash is a big, unmistakable burst with a strong smear, and its small, high-contrast silhouette stays legible in every frame. A has good motion cues (lean, scarf, dust), but its turns smear through rotation angles, its dash looks timid, and its blue-on-dark character often blends into the scene. Overall B looks slightly tighter and more responsive.
